evidence: paper: \sup_{0 < X \le X_i} \big\| \mathcal{A}_X (U_{\mathrm{r}}) - U_* \big\|_{C^k_\eta} \;\le\; \sup_{0 \le X \le X_i} \big\| U_{\mathrm{r}} - U_* \big\|_{C^k_\eta}

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's display says the radial average 𝒜_X is a contraction towards the constant-in-X comparison value U_*, in the C^k_η norm, uniformly for 0 < X ≤ X_i. Lean states this at k = 0 and k = 1 in one declaration: normalized_history_bounds takes sup-over-holdRegion hypotheses on U_r − U_* and on ∂_η U_r − ∂_η U_* (with U_* = NaturalAxisData.U j η, X-independent as in the paper, and ∂_η U_* = 4) and concludes the same bound for 𝒜_X U_r and for 𝒜_X(∂_η U_r), for every point of holdRegion = Icc 0 110 ×ˢ Icc (−1) 1, i.e. with the paper's sup over 0 < X ≤ X_i = 110 and over η already taken. Its engine is average_error_bound, which is the paper's inequality one scalar field at a time and pointwise in X: if |Λ(F(tX,η) − b)| ≤ B for all t ∈ [0,1] then |Λ(average F (X,η) − b)| ≤ B (Λ is a free positive scale; take Λ = 1). For k ≥ 2 the rewriting is: apply average_error_bound to F = ∂_η^k U_r and b = ∂_η^k U_*(η), move the k parameter derivatives through the average with parameterPartial_average, then take sup over X ∈ (0,X_i] and η ∈ [−1,1]; the right-hand side only grows because [0,X] ⊆ [0,X_i]. The one step Lean does not package is the iterated (k-fold) form of parameterPartial_average — only the single-order commutation is a lemma, though the analogous induction is carried out for `primitive` in ReferenceUniformJets.etaJet_primitive. Note the paper's C^k_η norm counts parameter derivatives only, which matches Lean's parameterPartial jets.
